name: How do you manage ventilation and cooking odors in an open-concept kitchen?

mainEntity.name: How do you manage ventilation and cooking odors in an open-concept kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ventilation requires a higher-capacity range hood with quiet operation and exterior ducting. Because cooking odors, heat, and airborne grease spread freely into adjoining living spaces, a hood with adequate cubic feet per minute (CFM) airflow is essential. Choosing a unit with low sone ratings prevents exhaust noise from overpowering television audio or conversation. If your cooktop moves to a central island, you will need either an island-mount ceiling hood or a downdraft vent system. Downdraft systems maintain clean visual sightlines across the room but may offer less capture efficiency for tall stockpots than overhead hoods.
acceptedAnswer.description: Install a high-CFM range hood vented directly outside, and choose quiet fan motors so conversation in adjacent living spaces is not disrupted.
